produtos.descricao: Llama-based safety classification model, fine-tuned to classify both input prompts (prompt classification) and LLM responses (response classification) against a configurable risk taxonomy (MLCommons, 14 categories). Open weights; Llama Guard 3 8B supports 8 languages and was optimized for tool call safety (search and code interpreter). Llama Guard 4 (12B) is the multimodal successor.

Compact encoder classifier (DeBERTa family) for detecting prompt injection and jailbreak in input text. Variants of 22M (English) and 86M (multilingual base), 512-token window. Adversarial-attack-resistant tokenization and an energy-based loss function for better out-of-distribution performance.

Configurable guardrails framework for LLM applications, based on the Colang language. Offers topic and dialog rails (thematic restriction and conversational flow), self-check of input and output via LLM, PII detection and masking in inputs/outputs/retrieved content, fact-checking and hallucination detection for RAG.

Layered prompt injection detector: (1) heuristics — filters potentially malicious input before it reaches the LLM; (2) vector similarity — stores embeddings of previous attacks to recognize similar ones; (3) LLM judge — a dedicated LLM analyzes the prompt. Canary tokens to detect leakage. The documentation describes it as a prototype without 100% protection. Repository archived (2025-05-16).

Input and output classifiers trained on synthetic data generated from a 'constitution' of natural-language safety rules. The prototype was evaluated over an estimated 3,000+ hours of red teaming with no universal jailbreak found. Declared overhead in the updated version: +0.38% refusals on production traffic (not statistically significant) and 23.7% compute cost.

Cloud service for detecting harmful content in AI applications. Includes Prompt Shields (text scanning for user input attacks on LLMs), text and image analysis APIs across harm categories (sexual, violence, hate, self-harm, with severity levels) and groundedness detection (preview).

Family of open-weight, instruction-tuned content safety classifiers. Version 1 is built on Gemma 2 in 2B, 9B and 27B parameters and evaluates inputs and responses against defined safety policies. ShieldGemma 2 (4B) labels images. The old documentation is marked as deprecated.

Protection API for GenAI applications (now under Check Point AI Security). The /guard endpoint screens text, user and LLM messages, and agent and tool interactions, with configurable policies. SaaS or self-hosted.
Prompt injection defense that uses an off-the-shelf LLM to detect and remove injected prompts from untrusted content. Reports false positives and negatives below 1% on the AgentDojo benchmark.

Open-source framework for validating LLM inputs and outputs, with a Guardrails Hub of pre-built validators (for example, toxic language and competitor check). Apache 2.0 license. In July 2026 validators moved to installable PyPI packages and hosted remote inference was discontinued.

Open-source library of input and output scanners for LLMs. Scanners include PII anonymization, topic banning, prompt injection detection, JSON validation and factual consistency checking. Archived project: the repository and associated models are no longer maintained.

Open-source security scanner for LLMs combining YARA heuristics, vector similarity search, transformer classification, prompt-response similarity and canary tokens. Declared alpha, experimental and for research purposes.

Enterprise GenAI security platform. The site describes sensitive-data protection with real-time response and Shadow AI visibility/discovery, plus security posture and compliance (NIST, OWASP) for agents; prompt injection appears as a product theme.

Guardrails engine for LLM applications and GenAI workflows (arthur-ai/arthur-engine repository; the old Arthur Shield page returns 404). Configurable metrics for real-time detection of PII or sensitive data leakage, hallucination, prompt injection attempts and toxic language.
